analysis.summary: Request for Proposals issued by the Town of Lebanon, Maine for design-build services for a new public safety facility of approximately 25,000 SF, including a 2,700 SF meeting room, dormitory space, administrative space, and related site improvements. The Town of Lebanon is issuing an RFP for Public Safety preconstruction services. The Design Builder is required to provide mechanical and electrical system narratives for subcontractors, manage the planning board approval process, and submit six paper copies of the RFP response to the specified address. Request for Proposals (RFP) cover letter for a new design-build public safety facility of approximately 25,000 SF for the Town of Lebanon, Maine, outlining facility requirements, space specifications, and submission deadlines. Overview of Phase 1 pre-construction requirements, including geotechnical work, permit applications, schematic plan development, a mandatory Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) submission deadline of April 12, 2024, and voter approval contingency. This text is a cover letter for a Design Build Request for Proposals (RFP), outlining the anticipated schedule from issue date through construction start in Summer 2024, contract and bonding requirements, submission instructions, scoring criteria, and voter approval contingency. The text outlines the evaluation process for selecting a Design Builder based on proposal completeness and team experience, notes the possibility of an interview round if no consensus is reached, and lists three application documents.

risks.title: Primary Site Suitability Uncertainty
risks.explanation: The preferred location at Merchant's Row may prove unsuitable upon pre-construction engineering analysis, requiring a potential location change to a secondary site.

evidence.excerpt: it is expected that the engineering analysis slated to take place during the scope of pre-construction services will disclose whether this location is suitable for the new facility.

risks.title: Uncertainty regarding Maine DEP SLODA Permit Requirement
risks.explanation: The RFP assumes site scope will not trigger Maine DEP SLODA permitting; if actual development scope exceeds thresholds, additional permitting and project delays may occur.

evidence.excerpt: We assume the size of the building and site development scope will not trigger the Maine Department of Environmental Protections SLODA permit requirement.

risks.title: Uncertain exact project programming and allowable dimensions
risks.explanation: The precise program and allowable building dimensions are left to pre-construction and Civil Engineering confirmation, which creates potential risk of scope changes or design modifications later.

evidence.excerpt: What that program entails exactly remains a task for pre-construction. It is imagined that the building will be approximately 25,000 SF in size (with a goal of having 4-5 bays), though Civil Engineering will confirm the exact allowable dimensions.

risks.title: Voter Approval Risk for Phase 2
risks.explanation: Proceeding into Phase 2 is dependent on voter approval in the June 2024 vote, introducing project continuation risk.

evidence.excerpt: Entering into Phase 2 (see below) is contingent upon voters’ approval in the June 2024 vote.

risks.title: Award Contingent on Voter Expenditure Approval
risks.explanation: The Design Build award is contingent upon voters approving expenditure for Phase 1 in June 2023, creating a risk that the project award may be canceled or delayed if vote fails.

evidence.excerpt: Design Build award is contingent upon voters’ June 2023 approval of expenditure for Phase 1.

risks.title: Conditional Interview Process
risks.explanation: If the selection team does not reach a collective decision upon initial review, an additional interview round may be introduced, potentially extending the decision timeline.

evidence.excerpt: if the selection team does not collectively choose a respondent as their Design Builder, the selection team may decide to interview selected candidate(s)
